title: Graphing and Interpreting the Integer Part (Truncation) Function
originalTopic: The Greatest and Least Integer Functions
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Describe the graph of the piecewise function f(x) = floor(x) for x >= 0 and f(x) = ceiling(x) for x < 0. Explain why f(x) is called the integer part of x.
finalAnswer: f(x) = \text{trunc}(x), \text{ which rounds } x \text{ toward } 0 \text{ and equals } 0 \text{ on } (-1, 1)

steps.title: Evaluate f(x) on Positive and Negative Unit Intervals
steps.explanation: For x >= 0, f(x) = floor(x) rounds down toward 0 (so f(x) = 0 on [0, 1), 1 on [1, 2), etc.). For x < 0, f(x) = ceiling(x) rounds up toward 0 (so f(x) = 0 on (-1, 0), -1 on (-2, -1], etc.).
steps.why: Combining (-1, 0) and [0, 1) produces a double-width zero step on (-1, 1) and unit steps everywhere else.

steps.title: Analyze the Symmetry of the Staircase Graph
steps.explanation: By the identity ceiling(-x) = -floor(x), f(-x) = -f(x) for all x in R, meaning f is an odd function whose staircase graph is symmetric about the origin.
steps.why: Rounding toward zero treats positive and negative numbers symmetrically with respect to the origin.

steps.title: Explain the Name 'Integer Part of x'
steps.mathExpression: x = \pm(n + r) \text{ with } n \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}, \; 0 \le r < 1 \implies f(x) = \pm n
steps.explanation: When any real number x is written in standard decimal notation, f(x) simply discards the fractional part after the decimal point and retains the signed integer before the decimal point (e.g., f(3.78) = 3 and f(-3.78) = -3).
steps.why: Rounding toward zero removes the fractional magnitude r in [0, 1) while preserving the sign and integer magnitude n.
